newsitem.title: USA: U.S. lawmaker says FAA lied on Washington airports.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lawmaker says FAA lied on Washington airports.

text.p: The head of a House subcommittee on transportation on Thursday accused Federal Aviation Administration staff members of lying to Congress on a project to consolidate the control facilities of the three Washington-area airports.

Rep Frank Wolf, chairman of the House Appropriations Committee's transportation subcommittee, said FAA staff lied when they told the committee that the proposed "Potomac Project" was not cost-effective.
"There was a planned strategy down there, you can see it, to mislead Congress," the Virginia Republican said.
Wolf said internal FAA reports show the "metroplex" facility in the Washington area would improve safety, provide more than $500 million in benefits and has a benefit-cost ratio of about 20 to one.
"The FAA has turned away from this proposal because one office in headquarters wanted to make their own reality," Wolf said.
An FAA spokesman said the matter was referred to the Department of Transportation's Inspector General as soon as Wolf brought it to the FAA's attention.
Wolf said he would take up the issue up with President Clinton's nominee to head the FAA, Jane Garvey.
